datasets.citation: World Money Roadmap, "U.S. Federal Reserve target rate change history", https://worldmoneyroadmap.com/data/csv/en/fed-rate-history.csv, as of 2026-11-21. Underlying data: Federal Reserve Board — Open Market Operations table.

columns.description: Date as printed in the Fed table (YYYY-MM-DD; often the day after the announcement)
columns.name: date_fed_table

columns.description: Change in basis points (1 bp = 0.01 percentage point), as printed
columns.name: change_bp

columns.description: Lower bound of target range (% per year; blank before Dec 16, 2008, when a single target was used)
columns.name: target_low_pct

columns.description: Upper bound of target range, or the single target (% per year)
columns.name: target_high_pct

datasets.description: Each date the FOMC changed the federal funds target rate (or range), the size of the change and the new level. Holds are not listed, as in the official table.
datasets.source: Federal Reserve Board — Open Market Operations table
datasets.title: U.S. Federal Reserve target rate change history
datasets.update_frequency: When the Fed changes rates (after checking the official table)

datasets.citation: World Money Roadmap, "Market dates — holidays, early closes, FOMC, CPI, jobs report, options expiration, ex-dividend dates", https://worldmoneyroadmap.com/data/csv/en/market-dates.csv, as of 2026-11-20. Underlying data: NYSE and Korea Exchange holiday notices, Federal Reserve FOMC calendar, U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics release schedules, Cboe options calendar, State Street distribution schedule (source URL on every row).

columns.description: Date (YYYY-MM-DD, local date of that market)
columns.name: date

columns.description: Reference month for CPI and jobs data (YYYY-MM)
columns.name: reference_period

datasets.description: U.S. and Korean market holidays and early closes, FOMC decision days, U.S. CPI and jobs-report release dates, U.S. monthly options and KOSPI 200 futures and options expirations, and SPDR ETF (SPY, DIA, MDY) ex-dividend dates in one table. Status = official, expected, tentative or calculated (rule-based).
datasets.source: NYSE and Korea Exchange holiday notices, Federal Reserve FOMC calendar, U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics release schedules, Cboe options calendar, State Street distribution schedule (source URL on every row)
datasets.title: Market dates — holidays, early closes, FOMC, CPI, jobs report, options expiration, ex-dividend dates
datasets.update_frequency: When official schedules are published or changed

datasets.citation: World Money Roadmap, "Trading days per month — U.S. (NYSE and Nasdaq) and Korea (KOSPI and KOSDAQ)", https://worldmoneyroadmap.com/data/csv/en/trading-days.csv, as of 2026-11-20. Underlying data: WMR calculation from the NYSE holiday calendar (Dec 23, 2025) and Korea Exchange holidays / official public holidays.

columns.description: Korea trading days (days; blank when the holiday list for that year is incomplete)
columns.name: kr_trading_days

columns.description: Status of the Korean figure (official or expected)
columns.name: kr_status

datasets.description: Trading days per month after removing weekends and market holidays (WMR calculation). U.S. early-close days count as trading days. Korean figures are expected until the Korea Exchange announces its holidays.
datasets.source: WMR calculation from the NYSE holiday calendar (Dec 23, 2025) and Korea Exchange holidays / official public holidays
datasets.title: Trading days per month — U.S. (NYSE and Nasdaq) and Korea (KOSPI and KOSDAQ)

datasets.citation: World Money Roadmap, "U.S. company quarterly and annual financials (SEC XBRL) — revenue, operating income, net income, diluted EPS", https://worldmoneyroadmap.com/data/csv/en/us-financials-sec.csv, as of 2026-11-20. Underlying data: U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) EDGAR XBRL companyfacts.

columns.description: Operating income (US$; blank if not reported)
columns.name: operating_income_usd

columns.description: 1 = fourth quarter derived from the annual total
columns.name: q4_derived

datasets.description: 10-Q and 10-K XBRL values filed with the SEC by the U.S. companies covered by WMR stock pages (fiscal-year basis). Fourth-quarter values are the annual total minus the first three quarters (q4_derived = 1; EPS not derived). Page tables round these values to billions or millions.
datasets.source: U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) EDGAR XBRL companyfacts
datasets.title: U.S. company quarterly and annual financials (SEC XBRL) — revenue, operating income, net income, diluted EPS

datasets.citation: World Money Roadmap, "AI investing experiment — daily paper-account value and cumulative return", https://worldmoneyroadmap.com/data/csv/en/ai-lab-nav.csv, as of 2026-11-20. Underlying data: WMR calculation (AI experiment execution engine, nav.json).

columns.description: Cumulative return since start (%, two decimals as on the page)
columns.name: cum_return_pct

datasets.description: Daily value and cumulative return since start of the paper accounts run only by AI. Hypothetical, not real trades, and not investment advice. Daily benchmark index values (third-party prices) are not included.
datasets.source: WMR calculation (AI experiment execution engine, nav.json)
datasets.title: AI investing experiment — daily paper-account value and cumulative return

datasets.citation: World Money Roadmap, "AI investing experiment — account metrics (vs. benchmark, risk, costs)", https://worldmoneyroadmap.com/data/csv/en/ai-lab-metrics.csv, as of 2026-11-20. Underlying data: WMR calculation (ai_lab_metrics.py, metrics.json).

columns.description: Benchmark code (spx = S&P 500, btc = Bitcoin, mix = ACWI and AGG blend)
columns.name: benchmark

columns.description: Benchmark cumulative return over the same period (%)
columns.name: benchmark_cum_return_pct

columns.description: Share of closed trades with a gain (%)
columns.name: win_rate_pct

columns.description: Cumulative trading costs (% of starting value)
columns.name: costs_pct_of_start

datasets.description: For each paper account: cumulative return, the benchmark's cumulative return over the same period and the gap, maximum drawdown, volatility, Sharpe, Sortino and information ratios, beta, trade count and costs, as calculated by WMR. With a short history the verdict is too_early. Not investment advice.
datasets.title: AI investing experiment — account metrics (vs. benchmark, risk, costs)
